psd_sdk vendored from https://github.com/MolecularMatters/psd_sdk
commit: f51449543273cbf12058ae92b230e0c4209f5066
License: BSD-2-Clause (see LICENSE)
Only src/Psd/ is vendored (the library); Samples/bin/build omitted. Files are LF here; upstream's
are CRLF.

Patched, not an unmodified snapshot. fire and 3D Review each vendored this commit and hardened it
separately; the two patch sets were merged when the crates did (fire-decode plan, FD3).
`fire-decode.patch` beside this file is the whole diff against upstream, and each hunk is marked
in the source: "FIRE PATCH" (fire's), "review-psd patch" (3D Review's), "fire-decode patch" (the
two merged).

- Psd/PsdAssert.h (FIRE PATCH): PSD_ASSERT throws psd::AssertFailure instead of calling assert().
  The library is compiled without NDEBUG, so a failed assertion on malformed input used to abort()
  the whole process; wrapper.cpp catches every exception at the C ABI. In the code the merged
  decode runs, the only asserts left are null-argument checks, so file contents no longer reach
  one; the patch stays as a backstop.
- Psd/PsdDecompressRle.cpp/.h (fire-decode patch, merged from review-psd P1 and FIRE PATCH):
  DecompressRle bounds every literal and run against both the source and the destination, returns
  false on a malformed stream, and zero-fills the rest of the destination when it does. Upstream
  wrote up to 127 bytes past the destination (and read past the source) on a malformed run.
  - The two apps differed on what a bad run means. fire zero-filled the plane and kept the image;
    3D Review refused the document. The merge refuses it (ParseImageDataSection fails), as a
    truncated file is refused. The zero-fill remains for callers that ignore the result, such as
    the layer parser.
- Psd/PsdParseImageDataSection.cpp (review-psd patch P2):
  - plane sizes in 64-bit arithmetic, refused past 32 bits;
  - every allocation null-checked;
  - the RLE payload bounded by the image data section it sits in;
  - uncompressed planes checked against that section before the first is allocated (a truncated
    RAW file used to have every plane allocated and zero-filled first);
  - a channel count of 256 or more refused rather than asserted;
  - a failed decode frees what it allocated and returns nullptr.
- Psd/PsdParseImageResourcesSection.cpp (FIRE PATCH): the DISPLAY_INFO resource sized its
  alpha-channel array as `channelCount - 3` (unsigned), which wrapped for greyscale documents
  (1-2 channels) into an allocation of ~4 billion entries. The merged decode never calls this
  parser (the composite's ICC profile is found in Rust, psd_layers.rs), so the guard is
  unreachable and harmless.

Header validation (bit depth, colour mode, channel counts, limits) is not a patch: it lives in
../wrapper.cpp, against limits the Rust caller passes in.

PSD layers are NOT decoded through psd_sdk: fire-decode parses the layer and mask section in
Rust (crates/fire-decode/src/psd_layers.rs), so PsdParseLayerMaskSection.cpp is compiled but
unreachable, like PsdExport.cpp.

Upstream since this commit (checked 10 November 2026): three commits to bfa1173 (2026-08-11), "Add
PSB Support. Add psd/psb open from memory support. add smart object support." They change the
document and layer parsers and the shared headers, but neither file the merged decode goes through
(PsdParseImageDataSection.cpp, PsdDecompressRle.cpp). Not taken: they would bring a rewritten
layer parser fire-decode never calls, and no PSB merged image.
